ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a simple radial feeder. A source or supply point is drawn on the left, connected by one horizontal line to bus 1 and then continuing to bus 2 on the right. A load labeled S1 is tapped downward at bus 1, and a load labeled S2 is tapped downward at bus 2. The diagram does not show any parallel branches, loops, switches, power electronic controllers, or other routing/control devices. Reasoning: The question asks whether the power flow distribution in this radial network can be controlled. In the shown radial tree, there is only one path from the source to each load. Power for S2 must flow through the line section from bus 1 to bus 2, and power for both S1 and S2 must flow through the source-to-bus-1 section. Since there are no alternative branches or control equipment, the flow distribution is fixed by the load locations and magnitudes rather than by controllable routing. Therefore, the power flow distribution in the network cannot be controlled.
